results.api: tokio-tungstenite reader -> Ndb::process_event(frame); Ndb::subscribe(filter) + SubscriptionStream -> Transaction + Ndb::get_note_by_key -> Note::id()
results.notes: Variant, unranked: nostrdb is a database, not a relay client; this row belongs with the app relay stacks (Notedeck/Damus) rather than the client libraries. Config: ingester threads = cores (default), verification on (skip_validation=false, default), and the optional indexing turned off with Config::set_flags(NDB_FLAG_NO_FULLTEXT | NDB_FLAG_NO_NOTE_BLOCKS | NDB_FLAG_NO_STATS) (nostrdb.h:23-25: no full-text index, no parsed content blocks, no stats). The LMDB write of every note remains: storing it is the library's job and the only way it delivers a note (subscription -> read transaction), which is why the row is not ranked. Each run writes to a fresh LMDB in a temp dir (an existing note would skip verification). EOSE is read off the socket before the ingesters finish, so the run ends at the last note delivered after it. The app's read path (subscription poll + read transaction + get_note_by_key) is timed. alloc_bytes counts only the Rust side (tokio-tungstenite, the app): nostrdb's C code mallocs outside the counting allocator and LMDB writes to a memory map.

results.api: enostr's path: tokio-tungstenite 0.24 task -> unbounded channel -> prefix check -> tokio::spawn per EVENT -> frame copy -> round-robin to nostrdb-style ingester threads (one per core) -> ndb_ws_event_from_json + ndb_note_verify -> app
results.notes: Variant, unranked: nostrdb has no relay client, so this is Notedeck's relay stack, built by the harness from the pieces Notedeck uses (HARNESS.md: a library with no client is paired with the one its users pair it with). Everything nostrdb's ingester does up to the database is kept, and only what storing needs is left out: the writer thread and LMDB, the id lookup in LMDB during the parse (ndb_ws_event_from_json gets no id callback), and the per-note malloc nostrdb makes because the note moves on to the writer (each thread reuses one buffer of max(frame length x 8, 4096) bytes instead). nostrdb's functions are called through FFI (nostrdb-rs keeps its bindings private): ndb_ws_event_from_json, ndb_note_verify (id recomputed and compared, then secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_parse + secp256k1_schnorrsig_verify), with a SECP256K1_CONTEXT_VERIFY context and a 2 MiB scratch buffer per thread, as its ingesters have. The socket is enostr's: tokio-tungstenite 0.24 over a tokio TcpStream (enostr also sets TCP keepalive, which does nothing on a 1-second local stream). alloc_bytes counts the Rust side only (tokio-tungstenite, the frame copies, the channels); nostrdb's parser writes into the reused buffers and allocates nothing.

results.api: tokio-tungstenite 0.24 read loop -> prefix check -> ndb_ws_event_from_json + ndb_note_verify on the reading task -> app
results.notes: As nostrdb-notedeck, but single-threaded: the task that reads the socket parses and verifies each EVENT frame itself, with no channel, spawn, frame copy or ingester threads in between, so it compares with the single-threaded clients. Variant, unranked, for the same reason as nostrdb-notedeck.
